Senses.Explanation: The summer retreat's enclosure, named by its ninety days — the boundary masters draw, keep, strain against, and sometimes dissolve outright. Lan'an Dingxu, at the retreat's start, verses the other side of the rule: ninety days confined, but for one idle beyond things, what confinement, what bond — a silk fan's breeze is enough, let mountains stay green and waters stay blue; Jieshi Zhipeng, closing the retreat, images the rule as netted birds homing to the nest and foxes set to guard tombs, and even three heads and six arms at the spot where birth and death cannot reach, overturning the awakening-hall, is still mooring to a stake; Huanxi Weiyi calls it cutting the crane to lengthen the duck and threading the ox through the horse — two thousand years ago the yellow-faced one drew the boundary on a needle point, and no one has crossed it since; and Xueyan Zuqin holds both horns: east corridor, west corridor, truly not one step moved — yet seated in this hall on this seat, he walks the whole world freely. Xutang Zhiyu, at the night assembly, names the strain: old seals unadorned, new rules in force — ninety days confined is splitting the jar to find the sky, three months protecting life is chopping the zither to stew the crane, leaving the determined nowhere to stretch; Muchen Daomin quotes the ancients' three cages — fish in the net, birds in the cage, the silkworm in its cocoon — then overturns them for his own war-torn, famine-year summer: Tiantong this summer holds no retreat and no confinement; Feiyin Tongrong dissolves the rule into the patch-robed life — roaming free by conditions, what talk of ninety days confined; that is carving ice to seek fire, steaming sand to make rice; and Chaozong Tongren spares no one on either side: at the ninety-day confinement, straining brows and eyes is labor squarely wasted; at the thrice-requested throne-talk, wagging tongues is mutual dulling.
